properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/29/2024
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8183524
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/11/2024
Comments: On 4/11/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 56 degrees, overcast and lightly raining when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Justin Green and HSE coordinator, Wayne Fletcher. Justin described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. They were currently drilling the production section on the 76HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,228 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,544 feet. Justin accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board.Due to recent rainfall, water puddles were present on the pad surface. I sampled a channel of water along the east side of the north perimeter berm that had demonstrated in prior inspections as having elevated levels of conductivity. The water field tested at 2.36 mS conductance near where a white residue could be seen on the gravel. The water field tested at 2.13 near the pad outfall in the center of the north perimeter berm and field tested at 2.11 mS as the water was running down the outfall. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin field tested at 2.15mS conductance. Water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 0.869 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 0.88 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. I did witness emerging vegetation in the constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Standing water was present in the basins.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.3. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.4. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/11/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8267702
Permit API: 051-21986
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2026
Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Gabonay National City Bank 6 well in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well. This inspection is being separated into 3 inspection reports due to the number of photos taken. The narrative of all 3 inspection reports are identical except for the references to photos. This is inspection report 1 of 3.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced. E and S plan is present on-site at the mailbox at the beginning of the access road.Well is tagged and posted. Production tank is observed within an adequately vegetated berm at this time. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time. The RCE is not installed as depicted on the plans. Minimal gravel is observed, which appears to be pre-existing. The access road does not appear to be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plans calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary." Four locations on the access road are experiencing erosion and sedimentation off of the access road (Photos 10-13, 18). CFS is also not observed in these locations despite the E and S plan call for CFS installed "as needed."There are 8 culvert crossings observed during today's inspection. Some ends of the culverts are blocked due to what appears to be recent soil and vegetation clearing off the access road. Some of the culvert crossings appear to possibly be stream crossings. A follow up inspection is being requested with Department Biologists to identify possible streams and/or wetlands. CFS is not observed to be installed at any of the culvert crossings except for the last culvert crossing closest to the site. The CFS at this crossing appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time, but is only installed on one side of the crossing. The E and S plans on site do not delineate or identify any stream or wetlands or crossings of any streams or wetlands, and no 105 permits are observed on site or at any of the crossings at this time. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.CFS is observed to be installed on-site near the well and appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. The location of the CFS appears to be placed in the correct area in relation to the site's topography, however the E and S plans depict the CFS to be placed on the opposite (East) side of the site. A small channel of stormwater appears to be leaving the site and passing through CFS at this time, however no sediment is observed leaving the site. The Department recommends the operator monitor and maintain this area as necessary to ensure CFS continues to function properly. Plastic matting is observed to be installed in 3 locations along the access road.The Department recommends the operator redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending consultation with Department Biologists.

Violation ID: 983711
Permit API: 117-22101
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Ward Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/01/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 well site located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 2/1/2023 at 1540 hours. The weather was 26 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in by Repsol.On 2/1/2023 at ~1335 hours, a release of ~5 barrels of produced water, ice and sand was discovered by Repsol after a line on a sand trap froze and split. Water, ice and sand was release to the pad surface near the wellheads onsite (photos #1 and 2). Sand, ice and dirt was recovered and placed in a 55-gallon drum for later disposal. The release mixed with onsite stormwater that was held in and around the well cellars. An onsite vacuum truck recovered a reported 1000 gallons of stormwater mixed with the produced water from the cellars and impacted area. I field measured all of the fluids in and around the impacted area for electrical conductivity utilizing an Oakton PCTS 50 meter. All readings ranged from 400 to 680us/cm today. Based on the reported release of ~5 barrels of produced water to the pad surface, new violations of the following are cited against API #117-22101 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.301Violations cited against API #117-22101 on 7/27/2022 remain outstanding at this time. I departed the site at 1615 hours.

Comments: On April 17, 2025 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Mountain View LTV 2 well located in Rostraver Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3715546 where violations were issued for a release and for IR 3882155 where violations were continued due to site conditions being unchanged. The LTV 2 site is located within abandoned coal mine land and therefore the well site is composed of coal refuge. Mountain View Operator Dave Lindahl informed the Department via email (documented in IR 3797419) that this abandoned coal mine land is to be remediated by the Department's Clean Streams Program and that this well site is included in their remediationplans. Mr. Lindahl also stated that what the Department observes to be a release from production equipment at the well site's entrance is actually runoff from the spoil piles upslope of the well site.During IR 3882155, the Department observed the spoil piles Mr. Lindahl mentioned, however, the Department did not observe any evidence of erosion channels or a distinct pathway that goes from the spoil piles and leads to the entrance of the well site where the release is observed to be. A distinct change in the ground level is observed in the release arearight next to the wellhead and separator piping, which further supports the notion that fluid from this production equipment is where the release originated. This in conjunction with elevated soil conductivity readings in this area lead the Department in IR 3715546 to again recommend the Operator remediate the release in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills despite the Clean Streams Program's remediation site plans including the LTV 2 site within it.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appeared to be unchanged. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it and a production tank was observed to be lopsided and sinking into the ground. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of the production equipment on site, however, the spill area documented in IR 3715546 still appears to be present. Fluid is observed to be pooled starting at the wellhead and proceeding to exit the well site and flow downslope. Based on unchanged site conditions, and the Operator's notion of this not being a release but rather spoil pile runoff, the Department collected soil samples for SAC 960 (General Chemistry) and UV (Ultra Violet)/IR (Infra Red) analysis at the following locations:Background 1 - Lat: 40.19595, Long: -79.76428 - In vegetation adjacent to well site 0.1249 mS soil conductivity readingBackground 2 - Lat: 40.19602, Long: -79.76539 - In coal mine refuse right below spoil piles 0.1388 mS soil conductivity readingLocation 1 - Lat: 40.19601, Long: -79.76466 - At base of wellhead where release appears to originate 0.539 mS soil conductivity readingLocation 2 - Lat: 40.19607, Long: -79.76459 - In spill pathway 0.782 mS soil conductivity readingAll samples were legal sealed and sent to the Department's Bureau of Laboratories in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.Based on today's inspection, violations issue during IR 3715546 shall be continued due to site conditions remaining unchanged.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of South Enterline Road in July 1997. Violations were issued during the previous inspection due to a spill from a hole in the bottom of the brine tank. Since that initial inspection, work has been started associated with the cleanup of the site. The brine tank has been removed, and contaminated soil has been excavated from the area of the spill. Conductivity readings taken during this inspection indicate that a small area of contaminated soil remains to be removed upslope from the current excavation area. Seed will then be needed in the spring. This site should be remediated as a visual cleanup.

Inspection Date: 3/11/2026
Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, and 4157162. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports. The narrative of both inspection reports are identical except for references to photos. This is inspection 1 of 2. A COA with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced.This inspection is being conducted with Aquatic Biologist 2s Christy Owens (DEP) and Miles Hegedus (DEP) to identify possible streams and wetland along the access road.Culvert 1 crossing (Photos 1-2) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The outlet appears to be blocked due to soil moved during access road clearing.Culvert 2 crossing (P 3-4) appears to be a stream crossing. The outlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 3 crossing (P 5-7) appears to be a stream crossing. The inlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 4 crossing (P 8-9) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch, however this culvert is not receiving water at this time due to the operator disturbing the channel causing water to be diverted further down the access road (P 10-12). The source of the water appears to be due to a seep which is causing early stages of wetland formation. The disturbed channel appears to be carrying fine sediment (Photos 10-11) towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen.Culvert 5 crossing (P 13-15) appears to be a stream crossing. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 5, however no sediment is observed entering the stream at this time.Just past culvert 5 on the inlet side appears to be a wetland (P 16).Culvert 6 crossing (P 17-19) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet of the culvert appears to be partially blocked. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 6. The erosion and sedimentation at this area appears to stop near the end of the culvert.Culvert 7 crossing (P 20-21) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet appears to be partially blocked and the outlet cannot be seen at this time due to brush.Culvert 8 crossing (P 22-25) appears to be a stream crossing. CFS is observed to be installed and functioning properly above the inlet side of the culvert. Upstream from the inlet of the stream and near the soil stockpile in this area, the Department observed newly moved soil that has been pushed into the stream channel.The Department recommends the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5 (P 8, 10-12, 16).The Department recommends removing sediment from the stream channel at culvert 8.The Department recommends the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.Violations were issued in IR 4157087 for accelerated E and S, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts in an inspection that was conducted earlier today prior to this inspection with Department Biologists. Therefore these violations are not included in this inspection report.New violations are being issued for sediment discharge into a stream, impact to wetland, and failing to identify wetlands and streams on the E and S plans.

Comments: On 1/22/2019 at approximately 1100, I conducted an incident response inspection of the Cosgray well site located in Franklin Township, Greene County in response to a reported spill of produced water. Specialized Professional Services (SPSI) responded to remediate the impacted area. An oil sheen was observed in one well cellar (37-125-27404). * Production fluid tanks were within secondary containment and appeared in good condition. Violations were identified during this inspection and will be assessed to each individual well.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/24/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 960284
Permit API: 081-21878
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/24/2022
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. The north ditch line channel is estimated at 400 feet in length with spilled fluid flowing an additional 25-50 feet off the north and east corners of the pad (photos 4 and 8). During discussions with Mr. Hood, when the well switch over occurs, down well fluid volumes are reduced and the blender valves must be adjusted to correspond to the reduced flow rate. Mr Hood indicated that the spill was caused by the blender operator falling asleep and failing to close a valve connecting the blender pumps to the working tanks during the well switch. Prior to site departure, Andy Steffee, Project Manager with Creston Environmental, arrived on site with a crew to begin conducting site characterization and sampling activity. Based on unknown volume of fluid spilled, Mr.Barbier indicated that EQT will immediately begin Act 2 remediation work. Well stimulation activity is expected to last into August at this location. Violations noted during this inspection and outstanding violations are extended.

Comments: On 5/23/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Folta well site. It was 58 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on location. When I arrived on site, I met with Chesapeake's company man, Joe Schulker who explained current operations as follows: Precision drilling rig 573 has finished drilling the Folta 24HC to TD. They have installed the production casing and Halliburton was on site cementing it in. Joe expects the rig to start drilling on the 25HC well tonight. The surface and intermediate have been drilled with the tangent, the curve and lateral left to drill. This is the last of the four new wells being drilled at the site. The six existing wells have been shut in for the duration of the drilling and completion process. Joe accompanied me on the site inspection. The drilling rig and all ancillary equipment is staged on secondary containment that is protected by drilling mats. The drill cuttings are collected, solidified, temporarily stored and loaded for disposal; all conducted over secondary containment. Chemicals are stored on secondary containment. The dry chemical additive area is staged on secondary containment. I did witness a 2' x 2' water puddle in the chemical additive area on secondary containment that field tested at 5.71 mS conductance. Joe said he would have the water cleaned up. I screened some of the soil on the unprotected pad surface around the chemical additive area with results at 0.6 mS conductance or less.I witnessed barite residue under the barite silos. Joe said he would get a crew worker to clean the area better.I did witness a rolloff dumpster marked as residual waste at the entrance to the site. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM has not been installed at the site. A new ESG3 was issued for the site on 5/4/2023. Construction on the ESG3 structures has not been initiated yet.Violations cited in inspection report 3520104 on 3/15/2023 are still outstanding for the site for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface after drilling operations had been completed.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake uses good chemical handling practices at the site and clean up any spilled chemical as soon as it is discovered.I left the site at 1130 hours.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/27/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8166301
Permit API: 081-20763
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lewis Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/27/2023
Comments: On November 27, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the Range Resources Cornwall Mountain 1-8H. This is to follow up with a reported spill by Range Resources on the afternoon of November 25, 2023 of approximately a barrel of production fluid. The production fluid was noticed bubbling from the well pad surface in the area of the buried dump line for the GPUs. The buried dump line from GPU 4 was immediately isolated. Range Resources found a small hole in the the buried dump line from the GPU to the production fluid tanks during the initial excavation where the bubbling was occurring. Upon arrival, Range Resources had dug three pilot holes along the dump line to aid in delineating the extent of the impact from the hole in the line. Three more pilot holes were dug during the inspection moving toward the production fluid tanks. The pilot holes were dug by a mobile high vacuum system. The last pilot hole dug, closest to the production fluid tanks, had a soil conductivity of less than 1,000 uS/cm. Range Resources conducted screening of the soil conductivity of the pilot holes and the conductivity ranged from less than 1,000 uS/cm to 4,650 uS/cm. Range Resources said that the production fluid that spilled seemed to follow the path of the dump line from the GPUs and did not appear to leave the well pad. DEP did not observe any seeps or erosion off the well pad edge indicating the production fluid had left the well pad. Kirby Steck with Range Resources said with digging the pilot holes they now know the extent of the area they need to excavate along the dump line. Range Resources plans to begin excavating the area around the GPU dump line to remove the impacted soil. The impacted soil will be placed in a roll off dumpster which was in containment. Once the area has been excavated, Range Resources plans on contacting Moody and Associates to collect the Act 2 confirmatory soil samples. The spilling of production fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface cause violations of the Clean Stream Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301.

Comments: On September 23, 2025, the Department conducted a Site Restoration Inspection of Diversified's Kennedy 4 plugged well located in Georges Township, Fayette County following a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) submission the Department received on 5/30/2025. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/5/2024. Therefore, the well site shall be fully restored by 1/5/2025 and a WSRR shall be submitted within 60 days of restoration. On 4/3/2025, the Department received a WSRR submission from the Operator, however that submission was denied due to Section G of the form being incomplete.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a graveled access road that leads to the Kennedy 4 plugged well site and a riser for an active pipeline. The Department utilized the plugged well's approximate GPS coordinate location to locate the plugged well and observed the area to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the plugged well's coordinate location. No erosion and sediment control features were observed to remain on site nor was any production equipment relating to the plugged well. Included with the 5/30/2025 WSRR submission was a signed landowner affidavit that states the landowner requests the graveled access road and a culvert to remain post-restoration. The 5/30/2025 submission, also references an email correspondence between the Department and the Operator on 1/24/2025, in which the Operator refers to the well site as restored, therefore a WSRR should have been submitted to the Department by 3/25/2025.Upon review of the WSRR and its supplementary documents, the Department is denying the WSRR submission at this time and recommends the Operator resubmit the WSRR with Section E filled out correctly. The Department also recommends the Operator include with the Well Site Restoration Report the Department's Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration form 8000-FM-OOGM0020 which can be found on the DEP's eLibrary along with the previously submitted Affidavit in lieu of a landowner signature on the form.Violations are also being issued at this time for failure to submit a WSRR within 60 days of restoration.

Inspection Date: 10/03/2022
Comments: On October 3, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and WQS Samuel Steingrabe. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3343707 where violations were outstanding due to deteriorated production fluid tanks that were discharging onto the ground, a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans. Also, no production reports have been submitted since 2014 per Department database. The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photos 2 and 3). No Emergency Response plans, or other required postings were onsite. The production fluid tanks onsite appear to have been replaced since IR 3343707 (see photos 5 and 15). Soil conductivity readings were taken underneath and around these tanks to determine whether petroleum products and/or production fluids were still present in the soil since IR 3343707. These readings were taken underneath the production fluid tank valves and in bare spots in their surrounding earthen berms. An additional reading was taken in a wet spot next to the tank farthest from the site entrance. The reading taken underneath the valve of the tank closest to the site entrance read 100 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken in the surrounding berm read 111 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). The soil conductivity reading taken underneath the valve of the tank farthest from the site entrance read 380 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). The one taken in a bare spot in the surrounding earthen berm read 640 Micro Siemens (see photo 11). The additional reading taken in the wet spot adjacent to the brine tank read 390 Micro Siemens (see photo 8). A background conductivity reading was taken in a well-vegetated spot at the well site entrance, reading 250 Micro Siemens see photo 16). No well tag was observed on the well or associated equipment with correct information (see photo 13), and the well API number was written on the meter box with sharpie. Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite (see photo 10). Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 14). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing. Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of October 3, 2022 and violations against the production fluid tanks have been corrected. However, outstanding violations that were continued in IR 3343707 due to production fluid discharge on the ground shall remain open since no NOV response or any information requested has been received from the operator to evaluate whether the release was remediated in accordance with chapter 78a. All other violations shall remain open as well since the rest of the site remains unchanged since IR 3343707.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/01/2024 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/01/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8177799
Permit API: 081-21938
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/01/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of 10 barrels of produced water. It was reported that there were 2 barrels off of containment and 8 barrels on containment. The release occurred from a low pressure line on a fracking pump while the line was being flushed with fresh water from an AST onsite. The mixture of fresh and produced water sprayed out as a mist over the secondary containment and the pad. The release was reported around 23:00 on 2/29/24.The affected area was about 60' southeast of the wells near the center of the pad. Tobias Welding and Machining began scraping the impacted area on 2/29/24. On 3/1/24, Penn E and R arrived and continued to scrape the area based on visual and conductivity screening. The scraped area was about 77' by 26' around and 2" to 4" deep. Penn E and R was in the process of setting up confirmation sampling for Act 2 remediation.DEP screened for conductivity inside and surrounding the scraped area. Puddles within the scraped area ranged from 0.84 to 0.96 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and the soil was below 0.10 mS/cm. Puddles surrounding the scraped area were 0.34 to 0.65 mS/cm. Soil conductivity readings were attempted outside the impacted area but the pad was too compacted.The removed material was being hauled to the neighboring Bieber Sisters Pad A where it was stored in a covered rolloff container on secondary containment. The material will remain on the pad until characterization samples are completed and it can be properly disposed of. Photo 3 shows the rolloff with about half of the removed material. The rest of the material was being hauled to the rolloff while DEP was leaving the site.Based on a conversation with Zac Subra, EQT, the initial reported volume of the release may have been overestimated. However, since an exact volume was not know EQT will still follow the remediation requirements of Act 2.It is recommended that the pad be screened when secondary containment is pulled to be certain that no produced water seeped under the containment as a result of the release.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), 78a56(a), and SWMA 301.

Comments: Weather was 65° and cloudy at time of inspection. Met with EXCO representative Chris Smith on location for inspection. Inspection was performed for the conclusion of a 72 hour pressure build up test. Well had digital pressure monitoring equipment s attached to the production tubing and the production casing. Production tubing pressure was 4500 psi and production casing pressure was 141 psi at time of inspection. The digital gauges on the 20x13 annulus vent and the. 13x9 annulus vent read 1 psi and 3psi respectively at the end of the 72 hour Pressure build up test (PBT) that concluded at 9:00am. The vents were opened into balloons and neither balloon popped. A photo was taken for reference. The balloons were removed after 1 hour and the 20x13 vent had 0% combustible gas detected with my Altair 5x gas meter that was calibrated on 5/12/21. The 13x9 vent had 100% LEL and 30% methane sustained for 1 minute. Both digital pressure gauges read 1psi at the end of the test like they did at the beginning of the test when the vents were open. No new violations were noted at time of inspection.

Culvert 2 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 8-9): Outlet still appears to be blocked. CFS was observed to be installed and functioning properly at both the inlet and outlet. Culvert 3 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 10-13): The inlet to this culvert appears to still be blocked. CFS was installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.Culvert 4 crossing - culverted for roadside ditch (Photos 14-17): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert still appears to not be receiving water due to operator disturbing channel and causing water to be diverted further down access road. The disturbed channel still appears to be carrying fine sediment towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen (Photos 18-20).Culvert 5 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 21-24): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this crossing, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.

Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township

Inspection Date: 11/21/2023
Comments: This site is in the process of being constructed for a conventional well. The template for the well site has been completed. The well site location and access road have not been stoned. There has been no drilling activity on site and the pit has not been dug. There was no activity on site during the time of the inspection. The drilling permit and Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) Plan were posted at the entrance of the location.The road leading to the well site location did not have culverts, sumps, or ditches installed as outlined in the E and S Plan. There were no temporary BMPs in place at the time of the inspection. Areas of earth disturbance associated with the construction of the well site location were not seeded and mulched.At the time of inspection, the site showed evidence of accelerated erosion. Sediment laden water was flowing parallel to the access road along the bottom slope of the constructed bank (pictured in Photo 1). The sediment laden water was ponding at the lowest point on the well site location (pictured in Photo 2). Stormwater and sediment from the well sites under construction up slope of Hastings SDT 47 OG Well were also contributing to the accelerated erosion at the site (pictured in Photo 3). Due to the volume of water, overflow from the low point was discharging off the site location (pictured in Photo 4). The sediment laden water was flowing through the woods directly discharging into Hastings Run (pictured in Photo 5). The operator, Steven Tachoir, was contacted over a voicemail to discuss the results of this inspection. He has been advised to install temporary BMPs to prevent accelerated erosion until the permanent BMPs can be installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. He has also been advised to seed and mulch the areas of earth disturbance associated with construction of the well. It has been proposed to the operator to meet on site to further discuss options for remediation. Follow up inspections will continue to occur until the work has been completed.

Due to the volume of water, overflow from the low point was discharging off the site location (pictured in Photo 4). The sediment laden water was flowing through the woods directly discharging into Hastings Run (pictured in Photo 5). The operator, Steven Tachoir, was contacted over a voicemail to discuss the results of this inspection. He has been advised to install temporary BMPs to prevent accelerated erosion until the permanent BMPs can be installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. He has also been advised to seed and mulch the areas of earth disturbance associated with construction of the well. It has been proposed to the operator to meet on site to further discuss options for remediation. Follow up inspections will continue to occur until the work has been completed.

Violation Code: 78a64a(c)3 - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT - Physical and chemical characteristics of all liners, coatings or other materials used as part of the secondary containment, that could potentially come into direct contact with regulated substances being stored, failed to be compatible with the regulated substance and be resistant to physical, chemical and other failure during handling, installation and use.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene

Comments: On 01/09/2020, I along with WQS Justin Najewicz, performed a follow-up inspection in response to violations issued during a previous inspection (#2952391). The issues noted during that inspection have been resolved. The leaking well head appears to have been repaired. The corroded production tank has been removed and replaced by a poly tank. Secondary containment has been constructed around the new production tank. The secondary containment liner has been fastened with screws into a corrugated pipe used to create a berm. The screws punctured the liner, compromising its integrity at/near the water level. There are several seams within the liner that do not appear to have been sealed properly. The secondary containment is also full of what appears to be stormwater to a level exceeding 10%. The Department recommends that the secondary containment be emptied and repaired/replaced in accordance with 78a.64.
